intro: You have come to Açıksaray, a rock settlement near Gülşehir in Nevşehir province, from the 9th–11th century. Here you will find dwellings and stables rather than churches. It is the clearest picture in Cappadocia of how a provincial Byzantine landowner lived.
history: Unlike Cappadocia's other sites, this rock settlement near Gülşehir is civil rather than religious. Its six separate complexes, dated to the ninth to eleventh centuries, hold dwellings, stables, kitchens and courtyards, each group arranged as the unit of a household or farm. Churches? There are few, and they are small.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rock dwellings and the façaded courtyards, then the stables with their mangers and the mushroom rocks.
facts: Did you know? The columns and arches cut into the rock faces imitate the front of a built mansion: hollowed out inside, architecture outside. And this was a place of everyday life rather than worship — dwellings, stables and courtyards, with few churches, and small ones.
outro: This brings our journey through Açıksaray to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these homes in the rock keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
